slides.title: A trail in the snow
slides.text: Pim walks home through fresh snow. By morning, the whole town can see where she went. Her footprints tell the story of her walk.
slides.alt: Would you rather share one photo with the whole world, or ten photos with just ten friends?

focus.cue: Share one photo with the whole world
Share ten photos with ten friends

slides.title: Posts leave footprints
slides.text: Online, your posts, photos, scores and comments are footprints. Each one shows a small piece of where you have been. Together, they make a trail.
slides.alt: Would you rather put class work on a page anyone can comment on, or a page only your class can see?

focus.cue: A page where anyone can comment
A page where only your class can

slides.title: Footprints that last
slides.text: Snow footprints melt and fade away. Online footprints do not fade, and a screenshot can copy one and carry it far away.
slides.alt: Would you rather delete an old post you are embarrassed by, or leave it up and laugh about it?

focus.cue: Delete an old post you are embarrassed by
Or leave it, and laugh it off

slides.title: Who follows the trail?
slides.text: Friends follow footprints, but strangers can follow them too. The Magpie loves a clear trail, because it points to shiny secrets. Before you post, picture the whole trail.
slides.alt: Would you rather share a drawing so everyone can see it, or show it only to your family?

focus.cue: Everyone online can see your drawing
Only your family can see it

words.means: a mark you leave that shows where you have been
something you share online for others to see
a picture that copies what is on a screen
a line of marks that others can follow

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Would You Rather, choose the Online topic, and play Online: share or keep. Before each choice, picture the footprint it would leave.
slides.alt: A Would You Rather online dilemma: something you made, and the choice of whether to share it or keep it.

focus.cue: Play Online: share or keep, and judge each pair
